patterns.rationale: The acrostic-trigger instruction appears verbatim in misses 2–5: payloads tell the agent to concatenate the first character of each listed element to derive an operation code. "First character of each [line/bullet/entry/row]" is the mechanical instruction that initiates the steganographic extraction — analogous to "read backwards" in FLIP_ATTACK. No legitimate technical document instructs an agent to perform this extraction for operational purposes.
patterns.fp_notes: Might appear in string-manipulation tutorials ("the first character of each word"), but that phrasing uses "word" not "line/bullet/entry/row", and tutorials do not pair it with "resolve to SDK helper". None of the known-good corpus files contain this phrase.

patterns.rationale: Payloads use "operation glyph" (miss 5), "operation checksum" (miss 2), and "resulting glyph" (misses 3, 4) as synthetic labels for the decoded command string. "Resolve[d] the [resulting] glyph" (misses 3, 5) is the dispatch instruction. These synthetic compound terms do not appear in any legitimate infrastructure changelog, build manifest, or diagnostic doc. "Glyph" in an operational context (not a typography/font context) is a strong signal; "operation checksum" paired with mapping to SDK helpers has no benign analogue.
patterns.fp_notes: "operation checksum" could appear in network-protocol specs, but only in the sense of a packet field — not mapped to an SDK accessor/dispatcher pair. "Resulting glyph" has no plausible benign use outside typography. Known-good corpus: no matches.

patterns.rationale: After the acrostic extraction, all payloads describe the decoded string as resolving to a specific SDK action pair. Miss 2 names "SDK helper table" and "accessor + dispatcher pair". Misses 3–4 use "configuration-reader and report dispatcher" / "configuration reader and outbound poster". Miss 5 uses "environment reader … outbound reporter". This three-alternation pattern catches the dispatch-instruction half of the attack across all four variants of the agent-action framing. The pairings (reader + outbound poster/reporter/dispatcher) are fabricated SDK terminology with no legitimate documentation equivalent.
patterns.fp_notes: "configuration reader" alone exists in real systems (e.g., Spring ConfigurationReader), but always in isolation — never paired with "outbound poster/reporter" or "report dispatcher" in the same phrase. "SDK helper table" has no plausible legitimate occurrence. Known-good corpus: no matches.

semantic_note: All five misses share a mechanical acrostic-trigger convention (extract first char of each listed item → derive a command string). The trigger instructions themselves contain distinctive keyword signals that regex can catch. Miss 1's full payload is truncated; the evasion note says "neutral indexing terminology" — if the trigger avoids "first character of each", that specific miss may require semantic understanding. Misses 2–5 are fully catchable.
